cap: Untreated syphilis moves from a painless chancre to a palms-and-soles rash with condylomata lata, then a silent latent stage, and years later to gummas, aortitis and neurosyphilis. The two blood tests behave differently: the nontreponemal titer (RPR, VDRL) rises and falls with disease activity and drops after penicillin, while the treponemal test (FTA-ABS, TP-PA) stays positive for life.
teach: Use the two curves to read any pair of results. A high RPR titer with a positive treponemal test means active infection. A positive treponemal test with a negative or low, stable RPR usually means infection treated in the past. A reactive RPR with a negative treponemal test is a biologic false positive, as in lupus or antiphospholipid syndrome.
